question: Are you compliant with GDPR, CCPA, and global privacy regulations?
answer: Yes. We comply with the European Union General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), the UK Data Protection Act 2018, and the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA/CPRA). We execute standard Data Processing Addendums (DPAs) incorporating the latest European Commission Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) for cross-border data transfers.

question: How do you handle Data Subject Access Requests (DSAR) and Right to be Forgotten?
answer: Customers can submit Data Subject Access Requests (DSAR), rectification requests, or deletion requests via our automated privacy portal or by emailing privacy@acme.com. All requests are verified and fulfilled within 30 calendar days at zero cost. Deletion requests purge data across production databases within 24 hours and secondary backup snapshots expire within 35 days.

question: What is your data retention and account termination deletion schedule?
answer: Customer data is retained for the active subscription term. Upon contract expiration or termination, customers have a 30-day grace period to download or export all records in standard formats (JSON, CSV). Following the 30-day window, production tenant databases are cryptographically erased. Encrypted backup copies are permanently rotated out within 35 days.

question: Who are your third-party subprocessors and where are they located?
answer: Our authorized subprocessors include: 1) Amazon Web Services (AWS) - Cloud hosting & storage (US/EU), 2) Cloudflare - Edge DDoS protection & CDN (Global), 3) Datadog - Infrastructure monitoring & SIEM (US), 4) OpenAI LLC - AI answer generation and embeddings (US), and 5) SendGrid/Twilio - Transactional notification delivery (US). We notify customers at least 30 days prior to engaging any new subprocessor.

question: Do you support regional data residency in the EU or UK?
answer: Yes. Enterprise customers can choose dedicated European data residency with all primary application clusters, PostgreSQL databases, and document storage hosted in AWS Frankfurt (eu-central-1) or AWS London (eu-west-2), ensuring zero data transfer outside the European Economic Area (EEA).
